tasks.question: How could cities reduce traffic and pollution?

models: One way to address this issue is to build more cycle lanes, which would help reduce traffic, and as a result pollution would fall.
A possible solution would be to invest in public transport, since this would ease congestion, making it easier to reduce pollution.
A key solution would be to introduce congestion charges, as it would directly discourage unnecessary car use, which means cleaner air.
One effective approach is to promote carpooling, because it reduces the number of cars on the road, and this would lead to less congestion.
One practical step would be to expand electric bus fleets, given that buses carry more passengers per vehicle, this would ensure lower emissions overall.
An important way to overcome this challenge is to reduce plastic use, because plastic production adds to emissions, which would ultimately lower pollution levels.

tasks.question: What could be done to help young people use social media more safely?

models: A possible solution would be to teach digital literacy in schools, since this would help young people spot misinformation, making it easier to use social media safely.
One measure that could help is to introduce stricter age verification, as this would limit access for underage users, particularly for younger teenagers.
One practical step would be to set screen-time limits at home, given that excessive use is linked to anxiety, this would ensure healthier habits.
An important way to overcome this challenge is to regulate harmful content, because unmoderated platforms expose young users to risk, which would ultimately make social media safer.
One effective approach is to develop better reporting tools, because it allows users to flag abuse quickly, and this would lead to faster removal of harmful content.

cues.cue: society / raise / awareness of online risks
models: A useful strategy is to raise awareness of online risks, since it helps young people recognise danger, helping to prevent harm before it occurs.

tasks.question: How could schools make learning more enjoyable?

models: One effective approach is to make lessons more interactive, because it keeps students engaged, and this would lead to better learning outcomes.
A possible solution would be to use project-based learning, since this would let students explore real problems, making it easier to stay motivated.
A key solution would be to offer more creative subjects, as it would directly appeal to a wider range of interests, which means fewer disengaged students.
One practical step would be to incorporate games into lessons, given that play increases motivation, this would ensure students enjoy the process.

cues.cue: schools / reduce / the amount of homework
models: It is important to reduce the amount of homework, in order to give students more time to explore subjects freely, otherwise enthusiasm for learning fades.
One measure that could help is to organise more field trips, as this would connect lessons to real life, particularly for practical subjects.

tasks.question: What can be done to protect the environment in your area?

models: A possible solution would be to plant more trees, since this would absorb carbon dioxide, making it easier to improve local air quality.
It is important to recycle more waste, in order to reduce landfill use, otherwise local resources will be exhausted.
A key solution would be to ban single-use plastics, as it would directly cut pollution, which means cleaner rivers and streets.
One practical step would be to organise clean-up events, given that litter harms wildlife, this would ensure a healthier local environment.
An important way to overcome this challenge is to protect green spaces, because they support biodiversity, which would ultimately keep the area liveable.
A useful strategy is to cut packaging waste, since it reduces unnecessary rubbish, helping to protect the local environment.

tasks.question: How could people be encouraged to eat more healthily?

models: A possible solution would be to tax sugary drinks, since this would discourage unhealthy choices, making it easier for people to eat well.
One effective approach is to teach nutrition classes, because it helps people understand healthy eating, and this would lead to better long-term habits.
One measure that could help is to label food more clearly, as this would let shoppers make informed choices, particularly for those managing their diet.
A key solution would be to subsidise fresh produce, as it would directly lower the cost of healthy food, which means more people can afford it.
One practical step would be to offer healthier menu options, given that convenience often drives poor choices, this would ensure better diets.
A useful strategy is to promote cooking classes, since it builds practical skills, helping to encourage healthier eating at home.

tasks.question: What could be done to reduce stress among students?

models: It is important to reduce exam pressure, in order to protect students' mental health, otherwise stress levels will keep rising.
A possible solution would be to offer counselling services, since this would give students support, making it easier to cope with pressure.
One practical step would be to spread out deadlines, given that overlapping tasks cause stress, this would ensure a more manageable workload.
One effective approach is to introduce mindfulness sessions, because it teaches students to manage anxiety, and this would lead to calmer classrooms.

cues.cue: schools / cut / the volume of homework
models: This problem could be tackled by cutting the volume of homework, which would give students more rest, and over time stress levels would fall.
An important way to overcome this challenge is to encourage regular breaks, because rest improves focus, which would ultimately reduce stress.
